title: Leaving Turkey and reorganising the band for Berlin
summary: Lehmann let the band out of its contract; Briggs went via Vienna to Berlin, returned to Paris to rebuild the orchestra and opened in Berlin in October 1925 with new trombone and guitar players.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And then the orchestra, we asked, I had taken the boys in with me to Mr. Lehmann. He knew what had happened, and I asked him, I said, "Mr. Lehmann, would you let us out of our agreement, because we do not feel like playing anymore in Turkey."
"We have a contract with you, it's a joint contract, but we hope you will let us out of the contract, because --".
He said, "I understand, I understand."
He even helped us. Most of us had booked the return passage by boat. But he said, "If some of you would like to go by train, you would -- I'll make it easy for you."
I'd taken lots of trains because I had to go through Vienna to my booking office before my Berlin. I went by train. And some
Briggs
of them had taken a boat leaving a little earlier, back to France.
And I -- from Vienna, I went to Berlin.
This was when?
This was 1925, '24.
Yes. End of '24, '25, yes. Beginning of '25. I went to Berlin to see the Barbarina and any address that I could get
I went back to Paris, because I had to make certain changes in the orchestra, reorganized the orchestra, I went back to Paris, and reorganized, and came back to Berlin about the 1st of October.
The 1st of October, 1925?
Right.
Then I had a three months contract.
Briggs 169
This was a new orchestra.
Yes, some new.
I replaced -- taken a new trombone player, because the other trombone player, he stayed in Turkey. He stayed in Turkey because he was in pretty bad health. And he stayed in Turkey.

And I came to Paris and I had taken a French trombone player. We had lost the guitarist. /He had said he didn't care to go to Germany, so I had taken another guitar player, which I changed right in Berlin, because there was an American boy in Los Angeles, Dickstein was the name. He was in Berlin.
Al Hughes, guitarist.
And Mr. TischeaeR told me that he was a very fine guitarist, so I heard him and taken him right after we opened.
